notes.text: It rained heavily all afternoon and the streets flooded a bit.
The forecast says sunny skies for the rest of the week.
A cold front is moving in, temperatures will drop tonight.
Thunderstorms are expected later this evening, bring an umbrella.
It's unusually warm for this time of year.
Snow is forecast for the weekend in the mountains.
The humidity today is unbearable, everyone is sweating.
Strong winds knocked over a few trees in the park last night.
Fog rolled in this morning and visibility was very low.
I tried a new pasta recipe tonight and it turned out great.
The bread didn't rise properly, might be the old yeast.
Grilled the chicken a bit too long, it was slightly dry.
Made a big pot of soup for the week, freezing half of it.
Roasted some vegetables with olive oil and garlic for dinner.
The cake needs another ten minutes in the oven.
Substituted butter with olive oil in the cookie recipe.
Marinated the tofu overnight and it absorbed the flavor well.
The new laptop takes forever to boot up, might need a factory reset.
Finally fixed the bug that was crashing the app on startup.
Upgraded my phone's storage but it's still running slow.
The wifi router keeps dropping the connection every hour.
Deployed the update to production without any issues.
My code review flagged a memory leak in the background worker.
Switched to a new password manager after the breach warning.
The API started returning 500 errors after the last deploy.

input.note: 25 short, deliberately varied-wording notes across 3 clear topics (9 weather / 8 cooking / 8 tech), authored fresh for this fixture. Used to both verify the n>=15 floor (first 5 and first 12 of this list, in order, are the n=5/n=12 sub-tests) and to empirically tune DEFAULT_CUT_THRESHOLD in packages/core/src/cluster.ts (0.85, recovering these exact 3 topics with zero cross-topic contamination -- see that file's doc comment for the full sweep).

assertion: clusterNotes() on the real embeddings' centroids of the first 5 notes returns null, and on the first 12 returns null (both below the n>=15 floor). On all 25, it returns exactly 3 clusters whose membership exactly matches the 3 true topic labels (no cluster mixes topics, no topic is split across clusters). Re-running clusterNotes on the identical 25-centroid input twice produces byte-identical (deepEqual) results.
